en.title: Epic Games Claims Jazz Jackrabbit Ownership Amidst Legal Dispute
en.summary: A legal back-and-forth has erupted between gaming icon Cliff Bleszinski and his former employer, Epic Games, over the rights to the beloved character Jazz Jackrabbit. The dispute highlights the complex nature of intellectual property ownership, even for foundational characters.
en.body:
## A Creator's Disappointment

**Cliff Bleszinski**, the visionary behind iconic franchises like **Gears of War** and **Unreal Tournament**, has found himself in a legal standoff with **Epic Games**, the company where he spent a significant portion of his career. The core of the disagreement centers on the ownership of **Jazz Jackrabbit**, a character Bleszinski created when he was just 17 years old. He brought the character to life in one of his earliest games, developed and released in 1994 shortly after he joined **Epic** in 1992. **Jazz Jackrabbit** quickly became **Epic's** breakout hit at the time.

However, after **Epic Games** recently incorporated **Jazz Jackrabbit** as a sprite in **Fortnite** Chapter 7, Season 4, Bleszinski expressed his dismay at being sidelined. He shared on his X account that after engaging legal counsel, **Epic Games** asserted full ownership of the character. Bleszinski noted the irony, stating, "After lawyering up Epic claims they fully own the rights to Jazz Jackrabbit and won't back down in spite of not having any paperwork to prove it (nor do I) in spite of the fact that they still pay me from sales of it on GoG (which means paperwork exists somewhere) and are still happy to monetize him in [Fortnite]."

> "Jazz was my first hit and will always have a spot in my heart. When I signed the contract with Epic I was a teenager and just happy to be making games and those documents have been lost to the sands of time. That said, I'm still somehow getting the occasional check from GoG.com that Epic is honoring, which seems to indicate that paperwork exists somewhere. I'm thankful to be paid on work I did 30+ years ago, however apart from random backpack cameos in Fortnite I was hoping I"

Bleszinski's statement to IGN further elaborated on the situation, emphasizing that he was a teenager when he signed his initial contract and that the relevant documents have been lost. Despite this, he continues to receive royalty checks from GOG.com sales, which he believes indicates that some form of agreement or paperwork must still exist.

## Fan Reaction and Implications

This dispute has inevitably resonated with fans who grew up with **Jazz Jackrabbit** and have followed Bleszinski's career. Many are expressing sympathy for Bleszinski, viewing **Jazz Jackrabbit** as intrinsically linked to his early creative vision. The situation raises broader questions about creator rights and intellectual property in the gaming industry, particularly when long-dormant characters are revived for new, highly profitable ventures. While **Epic Games** has not officially commented beyond their legal stance, the narrative that a foundational character is now subject to corporate ownership claims, despite the creator's ongoing connection through royalties, strikes a chord with a community that values the personal touch of game development.

## What's Next

Details regarding the specific legal arguments or any potential resolution remain scarce. It is unclear if Bleszinski intends to pursue further legal action or if a private agreement can be reached. Fans will be watching closely to see how this legal tussle unfolds and what it might mean for the future of **Jazz Jackrabbit** and other classic characters.

content_raw: Cliff Bleszinski, longtime Epic Games developer and the renowned designer of Gears of War and Unreal Tournament, hit a legal wall when trying to secure the rights to one of his very first game characters, Jazz Jackrabbit, from his former employer. Bleszinski says he created Jazz Jackrabbit when he was about 17. He turned the character into the star of one of his very first video games, which he developed and released in 1994 after he joined Epic in 1992. Jazz became Epic's biggest hit at the time. Now, though, after Epic added Jazz to Fortnite as a Sprite in Chapter 7, Season 4 earlier this year, Bleszinski expressed disappointment at being shut out of his character by Epic after a legal back-and-forth. "After lawyering up Epic claims they fully own the rights to Jazz Jackrabbit and won't back down in spite of not having any paperwork to prove it (nor do I) in spite of the fact that they still pay me from sales of it on GoG (which means paperwork exists somewhere) and are still happy to monetize him in [Fortnite]," Bleszinski posted on his X account. "So, if I get around to doing a new one expect the "spiritual sequel" route. Business is business, I suppose. My first sketches from high school here. Hell, must have been 17 when I doodled these." Here they are: Bleszinski issued a statement to IGN: "Jazz was my first hit and will always have a spot in my heart. When I signed the contract with Epic I was a teenager and just happy to be making games and those documents have been lost to the sands of time. That said, I'm still somehow getting the occasional check from GoG.com that Epic is honoring, which seems to indicate that paperwork exists somewhere. I'm thankful to be paid on work I did 30+ years ago, however apart from random backpack cameos in Fortnite I was hoping I could see to a proper revival of Jazz, either by my own hand or with a trusted partner. I pursued the proper legal path which ultimately led to a dead end - 'rights hell.' At the end of the day business is business and should I pursue anything Jazz-like in the future it would have to be in the 'spiritual successor' category. I'm still convinced no one has truly cracked the code of arcadey first-person platforming!" Jazz Jackrabbit isn't the only one of Bleszinski's creations to be active after a long hiatus lately. The Gears of War franchise returned to Xbox consoles last month with the excellent Gears of War: E-Day, a prequel to Bleszinski's 2006 original game. E-Day was the first new Gears game since 2019's Gears 5.
